# Postmortem

`customer_support.escalation_and_incident.postmortem` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**What made this possible, what made it last as long as it did, and what changes so the next one is shorter?**


> Turning something that already went wrong into a system that fails differently next time. The output is a changed system, not a document: a postmortem carrying actions with no named owner and no date is a memoir, and it will be cited approvingly for years while the same incident recurs. Blamelessness is not politeness — it is the only mechanism that produces a true timeline, because people who expect consequences report a defensible version rather than an accurate one. Support postmortems characteristically stop at the technical cause and skip the detection and communication failures, which is why the second occurrence is handled just as badly as the first even though the bug was genuinely fixed.

> Stub — identity, judgement and load-set only. Promote by adding outcomes, failure_modes (the ownerless action list, the single root cause where there were several contributing conditions, the timeline reconstructed from memory rather than artefacts, the review that examines the fix and never the detection lag, and the action that is "add more monitoring" with no named signal), playbooks, heuristics with a why on each, mental_models, decision_frameworks, kpis and handoffs, following escalation-management/capability.yaml in this folder. This is the only capability in the subdomain with a scoped object — customer_support.obj.postmortem.postmortem — and it is scoped rather than core precisely because nothing else in the domain should be reading a postmortem document; the moment a second capability wants it, that is a signal the findings are not flowing back as issues and root_causes the way they should.
